subject: Polity
topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: Who appoints the Chief Minister of a state?

options.text: The Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.explanation: The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor (Article 164). By convention, the Governor appoints the leader of the majority party/coalition in the Legislative Assembly. The other ministers are also appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: The Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers are collectively responsible to:
questions.explanation: Under Article 164, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha). This means the ministry stays in power only as long as it enjoys the confidence (majority) of the Assembly; if it loses a no-confidence motion, it must resign. This is the essence of the parliamentary system at the state level.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: Can a person who is not a member of the state legislature be appointed Chief Minister?

options.text: Yes, but they must get elected to the legislature within 6 months
Only with the President's special permission

questions.explanation: A non-member can be appointed Chief Minister, but they must become a member of the state legislature within 6 months, failing which they cease to be CM (Article 164(4)). This applies to any minister, not just the CM. They can be a member of either the Assembly or, where it exists, the Legislative Council.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: Who was the first woman Chief Minister of an Indian state?
questions.explanation: Sucheta Kripalani became the first woman Chief Minister of an Indian state, serving as CM of Uttar Pradesh (1963–1967). Jayalalithaa (Tamil Nadu), Mayawati (UP), and Sheila Dikshit (Delhi) were later prominent woman Chief Ministers.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: The Chief Minister acts as the principal link between the Governor and the:
questions.explanation: The Chief Minister is the principal link/channel of communication between the Governor and the State Council of Ministers (Article 167). The CM communicates the decisions of the Council to the Governor and furnishes information that the Governor calls for. The CM is the head of the state government (the Governor being the nominal head).
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: Which article deals with the duties of the Chief Minister regarding furnishing information to the Governor?
questions.explanation: Article 167 lays down the duties of the Chief Minister: to communicate to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers, to furnish information the Governor calls for, and to submit for the Council's consideration any matter on which a minister has decided but the Council has not considered. Article 164 deals with appointment; Article 163 with the Council aiding the Governor.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: The 91st Constitutional Amendment (2003) limited the size of the state Council of Ministers (including the CM) to a maximum of:

options.text: 10% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly
20% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly
15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly (with a minimum of 12)
25% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly

questions.explanation: The 91st Amendment (2003) capped the state Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, at 15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly, subject to a minimum of 12 ministers. This was introduced to curb the practice of forming jumbo ministries to prevent defections. At the Centre, the cap is 15% of the Lok Sabha strength.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: The oath of office to the Chief Minister is administered by:
questions.explanation: The Governor administers the oath of office and secrecy to the Chief Minister and other ministers (Article 164). This parallels the President administering the oath to the Prime Minister at the Centre. The CM swears allegiance to the Constitution and to discharge duties faithfully.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: If the Chief Minister resigns or dies, what happens to the Council of Ministers?

options.text: The entire Council of Ministers falls/dissolves
The Governor takes over as CM

questions.explanation: Since the Council of Ministers is headed by the Chief Minister, the resignation or death of the CM results in the fall (collapse) of the entire Council of Ministers. The other ministers cannot continue. A new CM must be appointed, who then forms a new Council. This reflects the CM's central, pivotal position.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: Who was the longest-serving Chief Minister in India (by continuous tenure)?
questions.explanation: Pawan Kumar Chamling of Sikkim is the longest-serving Chief Minister in India by continuous tenure, holding office from 1994 to 2019 (about 24 years and 5 months). Jyoti Basu of West Bengal (1977–2000, ~23 years) held the record before him. Naveen Patnaik (Odisha) has also had a very long tenure.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: The salary and allowances of the Chief Minister are determined by:
questions.explanation: The salary and allowances of the Chief Minister (and other ministers) are determined by the state legislature from time to time (Article 164). There is no fixed constitutional amount. The CM is also entitled to the allowances available to a member of the legislature.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: Which category of ministers is NOT part of the typical three-tier state Council of Ministers?
questions.explanation: The state Council of Ministers typically has three ranks: Cabinet Ministers (head major departments, part of the cabinet), Ministers of State (independent charge or attached), and Deputy Ministers (assist). Parliamentary Secretaries are NOT constitutional ministers — courts have struck down such appointments as attempts to bypass the 91st Amendment's 15% cap (an 'office of profit' issue).
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: In a state with a bicameral legislature, the Chief Minister:

options.text: Can be a member of either the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council
Must always be a member of the Legislative Assembly only
Must be a member of the Legislative Council only
Need not be a member of either house ever

questions.explanation: The Chief Minister can be a member of either the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) or the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad), where the latter exists. Several CMs have governed while being members of the Council. However, if not a member of either house at appointment, the 6-month rule applies (Article 164(4)).
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: The principle of 'collective responsibility' of the Council of Ministers means:

options.text: Each minister is responsible only for their own department
The ministers swim and sink together; a vote of no-confidence against the Council leads to the resignation of all ministers
Ministers are responsible to the Governor individually
Only the Chief Minister is responsible to the Assembly

questions.explanation: Collective responsibility (Article 164) means the entire Council of Ministers is jointly accountable to the Legislative Assembly — they 'swim and sink together'. A cabinet decision binds all ministers, who must publicly support it or resign. If the Assembly passes a no-confidence motion, the whole Council must resign, not just one minister.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: Who appoints the ministers of a state (other than the Chief Minister)?

options.text: The Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister

questions.explanation: The other ministers are appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister (Article 164). The CM thus effectively selects the team, but the formal appointment is made by the Governor. The ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor (which in practice means as long as they have the CM's support and the Assembly's confidence).
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: There is no fixed term for the Chief Minister. The CM remains in office:

options.text: As long as the CM enjoys the confidence/majority of the Legislative Assembly

questions.explanation: The Chief Minister does not have a fixed term and holds office as long as they enjoy the confidence (majority support) of the Legislative Assembly. If the CM loses majority (e.g., through a no-confidence motion or defections), they must resign or be dismissed. Technically the CM holds office 'during the pleasure of the Governor', but this pleasure is tied to Assembly confidence.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: Which of the following is a key power of the Chief Minister with respect to the Council of Ministers?

options.text: To recommend the allocation and reshuffling of portfolios among ministers

questions.explanation: The Chief Minister recommends to the Governor the allocation and reshuffling of portfolios among ministers, presides over Cabinet meetings, guides and coordinates the ministers, and can recommend the dismissal of a minister (or advise them to resign). The CM is the real head of the state government, steering its policies.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: In Union Territories with a legislature (like Delhi and Puducherry), the head of the council of ministers is called the:
questions.explanation: Union Territories with a legislature (Delhi — NCT, Puducherry, and Jammu & Kashmir) have a Chief Minister heading the council of ministers, who aids and advises the Lieutenant Governor (LG)/Administrator. The relationship between the elected CM and the centrally-appointed LG (especially in Delhi) has been a subject of legal disputes and constitutional interpretation.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: Who was the first Chief Minister of independent India's state to also later become the Prime Minister of India?

options.text: All of the above served as CMs and later as PM

questions.explanation: Several Prime Ministers were earlier Chief Ministers: Morarji Desai (Bombay State), Charan Singh (Uttar Pradesh), P.V. Narasimha Rao (Andhra Pradesh), H.D. Deve Gowda (Karnataka), and Narendra Modi (Gujarat). Lal Bahadur Shastri held state ministerial posts in UP. So the CM-to-PM path has been taken by multiple leaders — option D best captures that several listed leaders served as both.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: The relationship between the Chief Minister and the Governor is broadly modelled on which central-level relationship?
questions.explanation: The CM–Governor relationship at the state level mirrors the PM–President relationship at the Centre. The Governor (like the President) is the nominal/constitutional head, while the CM (like the PM) is the real executive head. The Governor normally acts on the advice of the CM-led Council of Ministers, just as the President acts on the PM-led Council.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: A Chief Minister advises the Governor to dissolve the Legislative Assembly. Is the Governor bound by this advice?

options.text: Never bound; the Governor decides entirely independently
Bound only if the President approves
Generally acts on such advice, but may use discretion if the CM has lost majority support, since advice from a CM who no longer commands confidence carries no binding force

questions.explanation: The Governor normally acts on the CM's advice to dissolve the Assembly. However, if the CM has clearly lost majority support, the Governor may exercise discretion — a recommendation to dissolve from a CM who no longer commands the Assembly's confidence is not binding. The Governor may instead explore whether an alternative government can be formed. This discretionary zone has produced several constitutional disputes.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: Under the anti-defection law (Tenth Schedule), if ministers/MLAs defect, the decision on disqualification is made by:
questions.explanation: Under the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law, added by the 52nd Amendment, 1985), the Speaker (in the Assembly) or Chairman (in the Council) decides on questions of disqualification due to defection. The Kihoto Hollohan case (1992) held this decision is subject to judicial review. Delays by Speakers in deciding defection cases have been a recurring issue affecting government stability.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: The correct way to test whether a Chief Minister enjoys majority support, as emphasised by the Supreme Court, is:

options.text: A floor test (vote of confidence) in the Legislative Assembly

questions.explanation: The Supreme Court (notably in S.R. Bommai, 1994, and later cases) held that the proper way to test a CM's majority is a floor test (a vote of confidence) on the floor of the Legislative Assembly, NOT the Governor's subjective assessment. This principle has been repeatedly applied during government-formation disputes to ensure majority is determined transparently and democratically.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: Which statement about a 'caretaker' Chief Minister/government is correct?

options.text: A caretaker government has full powers to make major policy decisions
A caretaker CM is appointed by the Supreme Court
A caretaker government (after the Assembly is dissolved, pending elections) is expected to handle only routine/day-to-day administration and avoid major policy decisions
A caretaker government can amend the state's laws freely

questions.explanation: A caretaker government continues in office after the Assembly is dissolved, until a new government is formed after elections. By convention, it is expected to confine itself to routine, day-to-day administration and refrain from major policy decisions or significant appointments, since it lacks a fresh mandate. This is a constitutional convention rather than an explicit provision.
questions.subject: Polity
questions.topic: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers

questions.stem: The phrase 'the ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor' effectively means in practice that:

options.text: The Governor can dismiss any minister arbitrarily at will, regardless of the Assembly
Ministers can never be removed once appointed
A minister can be removed by the Governor, but in practice this 'pleasure' operates on the advice of the Chief Minister and is tied to the Assembly's confidence in the government
Only the President can remove a state minister

questions.explanation: Although Article 164 says ministers hold office 'during the pleasure of the Governor', in a parliamentary system this pleasure is not exercised arbitrarily. In practice, a minister is removed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister, and the government as a whole survives only while it retains the Assembly's confidence. The Governor cannot, on his own whim, dismiss an individual minister against the CM's wishes.
